description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of five different methods—labeled Base, MEND, FT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic x-axis ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 30% to 55%. The 'Base' method is shown as a black line with circle markers, starting at approximately 28% accuracy and increasing slightly to about 32% over the range. The 'MEND' method is depicted as a brown line with diamond markers, beginning at about 36% and rising to around 45%. The 'FT' method is a blue line with triangle markers, starting near 32% and ending at approximately 38%. The 'IKE' method is a red line with triangle markers, starting at about 33% and increasing to roughly 41%. The 'ROME' method is shown as a green line with square markers, beginning at approximately 44% and steadily increasing to nearly 57%. All lines show a general upward trend, with ROME consistently achieving the highest accuracy across the entire range of co-occurrence numbers.
